analyst_view.overall: Early view: Brentford lost 2-0 at Brighton after Igor Thiago was sent off in the 23rd minute, and the brief lists him as missing here; I could not confirm the length of his ban. Everton are sixth after back-to-back wins, the latest 3-1 against Coventry with two goals from Thierno Barry, and Moyes has kept Jack Grealish out of the squad for a breach of club discipline.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. I lean slightly lower: Brentford are likely to be without their main striker Thiago and have won one of their last five, and Everton's away win at Newcastle was a 1-0. A tight game suits both sides' current form.

corners.text: The numbers say 10 corners, split fairly evenly. The game looks balanced, as the win-draw-loss numbers suggest, and nothing in the team news shifts that, so I keep the site's figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. Brentford had Ajer and Schade booked as well as Thiago's red at Brighton, while Everton picked up just one booking against Coventry. With no referee named, I stay close to the numbers.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.7 shots. I lean lower: without Thiago, Brentford lose their focal point up front, and Fabio Carvalho and Antoni Milambo were also out before the break. Everton's 1-0 at Newcastle suggests Moyes is happy to keep away games tight.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target. I lean slightly lower for the same reason: Brentford's main finisher is likely missing and Everton have kept their away games tight. Barry's form is the main threat to this view.
